gaps.stack_core_full_sweep: The full stack-core suite (98 files, 2419 collected) did NOT complete at this close — the third close running. It was attempted with per-test -v naming and a watchdog, and reached 892 of 2419 before being stopped to free the contended host. IT IS NOT DEADLOCKED — it advanced 8 tests in 240 s (~2/min) while three other review agents ran the same suites concurrently. THE SLOW REGION IS NAMEABLE: it crawled through tests/test_fence_provenance.py, whose arms each spawn subprocesses that walk the whole corpus. M255 already recorded the shape ('a 276-test unit suite taking 3.5-4.5 min is SLOW, and the cost is concentrated in the corpus-walking fences'); at 2419 tests that cost is now the reason the suite cannot be swept. 13 failures had accrued by test 892, in 6 modules (test_anchor_subject_census_m257x 5, test_blocking_state_guard 2, test_decommissioned_instruction_guard 2, test_battery_stage 1, test_claim_census_substrate_m257x 1, test_clone_pin_guard 1) — the census module's own 11 had not been reached yet (it sorts after test_fence_provenance), so the full-sweep failure total is >= 24 and was never established. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: run it ALONE on an idle host with pytest-timeout wired per-test and record per-test durations; or shard tests/test_fence_provenance.py and the other corpus-walking fences into their own lane. Until then stack-core is reported BY SCOPED MODULE and must never be described as 'swept clean'.
